comparator.name: Mechanical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Mechanical Engineering/Marine Technology OER curriculum table (PDF page index 25), rechecked on 15 October 2026, establishes the 25 stored components and their 180-EC total. Each of Years 1 and 2 contains ten 6-EC units. Year 1 separately credits Design Projects 1, 2, 3A and 3B; the public page groups 3A and 3B as one third design project. Year 2 contains four project units: Advanced Engineering Design, Process Engineering and Thermodynamics, Robotics, and Materials Science. Year 3 preserves the approved 30-EC minor and requires Systems and Control Engineering 6 EC, Integrated Mechanical Systems 6 EC, Engineer and Society 4 EC and the Bachelor Final Project 14 EC. Mathematics/mechanics subparts remain within their credited parent units. No named route requires selection. The previously verified component identities, weights and neutral route decision are preserved. Current review1November2026 also verifies Appendix7.3: BEP entry requires all first-year courses and54EC from year2; ordinary second-semester start in week3, with results through the second Q2 examination period. Generic minor subject to university/board approval.
components: Genuine first-semester minor space preserved from the official curriculum.

audience.programmeDescription: In this Dutch-taught degree, students analyse and design mechanical devices and systems. They study mathematics, mechanics, materials, thermal and fluid processes and control through theory, laboratories and design projects, with a minor and a final research or design project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination develops models of dynamic systems and applies them to motion planning, feedback and robotics. Delft develops these subjects through mechanical design and also requires mechanics of materials, thermodynamics, fluid flow and fabrication.

curriculum.limitation: The 30-EC minor remains open subject to approval. The 14-EC final project requires all first-year courses and at least 54EC from year two.

componentNotes.me-y3-minor: A university-approved thematic minor or an individual minor approved by the examination board.
componentNotes.me-y3-project: Compulsory 14-EC research or design project. The ordinary start is in week three of semester two; entry requires all first-year courses and at least 54EC from year two.

core: Mechanical science, materials, thermal and fluid processes, manufacturing, integrated engineering design and experimental projects
Calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, probability, numerical methods, signals and mathematical system models
Robotics, motion planning, automated systems, computational control and reliable machine behaviour
Product design, modelling, prototyping, experimental evaluation and lifecycle-sensitive development
adjacent: Energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy assessment, repair/reuse, circular resources and sustainable technical systems
questions: How can mathematical models and computational methods support automated motion, perception and technical decisions?
How can technical systems reduce energy demand and material use throughout product lifecycles?

candidates.label: Energy-efficient technologies and circular resource systems
candidates.reason: Renewable energy and circular materials are feasible UCR subjects, but this Delft route centres its energy teaching on heat, fluid flow and process thermodynamics. Generic energy governance does not establish a distinct second comparison.

trace: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one.
Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty.
Introduces formal logic, abstract mathematical reasoning and proof.
Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments.
Studies computer networks and operating systems as the infrastructure for communication and resource management.
Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time.
Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data.
Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes.
Examines how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognize structures and objects.
Develops neural-network theory and practical implementation in Python, Keras and TensorFlow.
Studies computational problems in robot motion and manipulation, supported by linear algebra, calculus and geometric modelling.
Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python.
Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems.
Develops linear algebra from systems of equations and matrix operations to vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality.
Develops numerical solutions to mathematical problems that lack convenient analytical solutions, emphasizing when algorithms work and how to validate their output.
Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions.
Analyzes continuous- and discrete-time signals and linear time-invariant systems through differential or difference equations, impulse responses and frequency-domain representations.
Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference.
Uses planetary boundaries to introduce scientific tools for understanding sustainability and human impacts on Earth systems.
Connects wave physics, chemistry and materials science to sustainability questions.
Develops life-cycle approaches to evaluating products, processes and services within a circular economy.
Teaches assessment of energy usage patterns and strategies for reducing consumption or transitioning to cleaner energy.
